newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's APV denies further MOL offer imminent.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's APV denies further MOL offer imminent.

text.p: The Hungarian privatisation agency APV Rt denied a report on Thursday that another IPO for oil and gas company MOL Rt was imminent but said there could be one before the end of the year.

"That is a red herring," APV spokesman Adam Dudits said of a report by the Platt's news agency saying financial advisers for MOL were expected to decide on Friday or Monday whether to offer an additional 2.5 percent stake in MOL.
"There will not be one in the near future, and that means not next week or month and not June, July or August," Dudits said.
Timing of another offering "depends on the international advisers and the international market," he said, adding that there could be one "maybe at the end of the year".
APV sold altogether 19 percent of MOL this month, placing 12.5 percent with international investors and four percent domestically, all heavily oversubscribed.
The global coordinators of the private placement this week called an overallotment option for 2.5 percent.
Dudits said APV was aware the Hungarian bourse was looking for more shares, but said APV would not be driven "just because the Hungarian market wants more".
After the just completed placement APV retains an estimated 39.7 percent of MOL shares.
